summary.primary_diagnosis: Deep vein thrombosis of the left lower extremity with pulmonary embolism
summary.hospital_course: A 68-year-old male with a history of COPD presented with left calf swelling and pleuritic chest pain and was admitted on 2026-09-01. Doppler ultrasound confirmed an extensive left femoropopliteal deep vein thrombosis, and CT pulmonary angiography demonstrated bilateral segmental pulmonary emboli without right heart strain. The patient remained hemodynamically stable throughout admission and was managed with warfarin anticoagulation. During hospitalization, he developed rapid atrial fibrillation with rates up to 150 bpm; amiodarone was initiated for rhythm control and his rate settled. Additionally, following a course of inhaled steroids, he developed oropharyngeal candidiasis and was started on a seven-day course of fluconazole. On the day of discharge (2026-09-06), his INR was 2.4 and rising, with the warfarin dose increased to 7.5 mg daily. Due to significant interactions with amiodarone and fluconazole potentiating warfarin, urgent anticoagulation clinic review was requested prior to the first post-discharge dose, with repeat INR recommended within 3 days. The patient noted that his omeprazole was stopped during admission and requested clarification regarding its restart.
summary.condition_at_discharge: Hemodynamically stable, rapid atrial fibrillation resolved and rate controlled on amiodarone, INR 2.4 and rising.

interactions.description: Fluconazole strongly inhibits CYP2C9, the main enzyme clearing S-warfarin. INR can rise sharply within 2-3 days, with a substantial bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid the combination where an alternative antifungal exists. If unavoidable, reduce the warfarin dose and recheck INR within 3 days with anticoagulation clinic oversight.

interactions.description: Amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism and its long half-life means the effect accumulates over weeks. INR typically rises with a delayed onset.
interactions.recommendation: Anticipate a warfarin dose reduction of roughly one third. Recheck INR within 3-5 days and monitor weekly for the first month.

interactions.description: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4, raising atorvastatin exposure and the risk of myopathy.
interactions.recommendation: Limit atorvastatin to 20 mg daily with amiodarone; counsel on muscle pain.

medications.notes: Pharmacist review required due to high-alert medications (warfarin, amiodarone), a contraindicated interaction between fluconazole and warfarin, a major interaction between amiodarone and warfarin, and an unreconciled pre-admission medication (omeprazole).

education.plain_language_summary: You were in the hospital for a blood clot in your leg and lung, a new irregular heartbeat, and a yeast infection in your mouth. You have new and changed medicines that help prevent clots and keep your heart beating regularly. You will need close follow-up visits and home nurse checks to make sure your blood thinner level is safe. Do not restart any home medicines that were stopped in the hospital without talking to your doctor.
medication_instructions: Warfarin 7.5 mg once daily: Take 1 time each day. This is a blood thinner to treat blood clots. Your dose was increased in the hospital. Your other medicines make Warfarin stronger, so you need frequent blood checks.
Amiodarone 200 mg once daily: Take 1 time each day to help keep your heart rate and rhythm steady.
Fluconazole 100 mg once daily: Take 1 time each day for 7 days to treat the yeast infection in your mouth.
Tiotropium 18 mcg once daily: Inhale 1 time each day to help keep your airways open.
Atorvastatin 40 mg once daily: Take 1 time each day to lower cholesterol and protect your heart.

Omeprazole 20 mg once daily (STOPPED): Do NOT take Omeprazole at home. This medicine was stopped in the hospital and left unreconciled. Do not restart taking Omeprazole unless your primary care doctor reviews it and tells you to take it.
activity_and_diet: Keep a steady diet when taking Warfarin. Eat consistent amounts of green leafy vegetables each day.
Drink plenty of water and rest as you recover.
Avoid heavy lifting or activities that could cause a fall or cut while on blood thinners.
red_flag_symptoms: Any unusual bleeding, such as bleeding gums, nosebleeds lasting more than 10 minutes, dark or black tarry stools, pink or red urine, or coughing up blood.
Sudden or large bruises that appear without any injury.
Sudden shortness of breath or trouble breathing.
Chest pain, tightness, or a fast or fluttering heartbeat.
New or worsening swelling, pain, warmth, or redness in your legs or ankles.
Gaining more than 3 pounds in one day or 5 pounds in one week.
caregiver_instructions: Daniel Adeyemi (son): Help make sure medicines are taken exactly as written every day, especially Warfarin and the 7-day course of Fluconazole.
Ensure the patient does NOT resume taking Omeprazole at home without doctor approval.
Help keep track of upcoming appointments: Anticoagulation Clinic on September 9, 2026, and Primary Care on September 12, 2026.
Watch for red-flag signs of bleeding, swelling, or breathing changes, and call for medical help right away if seen.
